entry_state: Partial purchase cessation retains a stopped reserve and sends subsequent owned-instrument changes to profit. Homogeneous proportional allocation is justified separately from the narrower origin-matched derivation. Expectation changes and unrecoverable losses release only the remaining signed reserve; gross settlement and liquidity checks close the conditional histories. General heterogeneous attribution remains open.
exit_state: The reserve transfers into inventory basis at purchase; subsequent sales and supported NRV changes track remaining quantities and allowance without recreating it. A net currency hedge retains gross revenue, expense and their recognition periods, including the stricter nil-position conditions. The chapter now turns to conditional award accounting and participating shares under a separately identified IFRS scope.
findings: The inventory close shows why prematurely crediting reserve to profit can give the same lifetime total while misstating interim inventory and earnings.
The subsequent-sale derivation removes the sold allowance before any recovery, preventing reversal for goods no longer held.
The net hedge example preserves gross statement lines and derives the two-period reserve of eight; it distinguishes reserve from a derivative asset or service income.
No new confirmed local defect. The component/rebalancing section closes with pricing, qualification and general allocation limits retained.
